text:
andrew: Quick update from pelican9b quant experiments. focused slices: multi-turn summarization, code completion, and casual chat. initial summary: int8 is a good latency/cost middle ground; int4 is much cheaper but shows regressive behavior on long priming.

sara: numbers?

andrew: microbench (normalized cost/token): fp16 p95=220ms cost=$0.012; int8 p95=180ms cost=$0.0095; int4 p95=170ms cost=$0.0061.

kai: quality metrics?

andrew: used hallucination checks + intent-pass. fp16 halluc=3.2% intent=93.5%. int8 halluc=3.6% intent=92.8%. int4 halluc=6.9% intent=88.1%. degradation tied to long instruction prefixes and KV reuse.

mira: so int4 risky for long multi-turn. possible mitigations?

andrew: routing by prefix length and cache-reuse heuristics works well. simple rule classifier hits ~92% on validation; routes ~60% traffic to int4 safely.

olivia: unit-econ if hybrid 70/30 int4/int8 on 1M tokens/day -> avg $0.00728/token => $7,280/day vs $9,500 (all-int8) vs $12,000 (fp16).

sara: product guidance?

kai: recommend "economy" tier = hybrid routing + disclaimer about long sessions; "pro" = pinned to int8/fp16. provide GTN scorecard: p95 latency, cost per 1M tokens, intent-pass delta vs fp16, and sample failure transcripts.

andrew: rollout plan: canary 5% hybrid rules x48h, check intent-pass & NPS proxy; if <1.5% delta, expand to 25% x72h; move to 60% after stable week. human eval of 200 multi-turn threads queued to catch subtle fluency drops.

ops-bot: autoscaler note: need "quant-variant" label for Q4 queues; eng-infra PR required.

mira: agree on cautious hybrid + routing-by-prefix as default rec. andrew will prepare scorecard + anonymized failure examples by EOD tomorrow.

andrew: ping @sara @kai when ready :thumbsup:

ops-bot: deploy note: feature/pelican9b-hybrid-route created (waiting eng-infra helm PR).
